parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented universal exposure (no facility/birth-sex rules, no border document friction), and hate-crime plus anti-discrimination provisions covering gender identity are on the books with documented police/prosecutor training and detainee-address guidelines. Against that: enforcement is documented as weak (complaints disregarded, attacks unpunished), the culture is strongly heteronormative, and the violence record — though severe in individual cases (2001, 2009, 2014) — is dated, capital-scoped and scattered, not patterned or state-directed (tier 4). Survey figures are LGBT-wide and expired, so they carry no current prevalence weight. No police targeting of trans visitors is documented; the 2019 officer assault prompted training rather than impunity. Resident-facing gaps (marriage bar, surgery-based ID change) don't touch a visitor. Thin data outside the capital and unresolved status of the 2019 guidelines keep this below the better-protected 0.65–0.75 anchors; absent documented visitor-facing hostility, it sits above the 0.55 tier.
